bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Quashes Invalid Nominations for Medical College Admissions Due to Abuse of Power. Chief Minister's Nominations Declared Invalid as Admissions Must Be Based on Merit Under Articles 14, 16, and 32 of the Constitution. In Favour of Prosecution Admin 2026-10-11 23:55:32 15 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The case involved a dispute regarding the admission process for medical colleges in Jammu and Kashmir, specifically concerning nominations made by the Chief Minister of Bihar. Nine seats were reserved for candidates from Bihar, with thirty-five students applying for these positions. A merit list was prepared by the Controller of Examinations, which included the petitioner, Surendra Kumar, but was overshadowed by additional nominations made by the Chief Minister based on recommendations from VIPs. The court found that this practice constituted a blatant abuse of power, undermining the constitutional principles of equality and merit. The court referenced a previous judgment in Suman Gupta v. State of Jammu and Kashmir, emphasizing that the selection process must not be left to the unfettered discretion of the executive. The court quashed the Chief Minister's list of nominations and directed the Government of Bihar to prepare a merit list from all candidates who sought admission, ensuring that the selection process adhered to merit-based criteria. The court also expressed concern over the recurring issue of power abuse in Bihar and ordered the respondents to pay costs to the petitioner. The decision reinforced the necessity of adhering to constitutional values in educational admissions. Headnote A) Constitutional Law - Admission to Medical Colleges - Abuse of Power - Constitution of India, 1950, Articles 14, 16, 32 - The Chief Minister's nominations for medical college admissions were quashed due to blatant abuse of power, and the court directed that admissions be based strictly on merit. The Government of Bihar was ordered to prepare a merit list of all candidates who sought admission, not limited to those who applied for the reserved seats. Held that the selection process must adhere to constitutional principles of equality (Paras 20-22). bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Upholds State's Educational Policy for Project Schools — Emphasizes Right to Education. Admin 2026-10-12 01:45:57 3 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The dispute arose from the State of Bihar's educational policy aimed at establishing Project Schools to improve access to education in backward areas. The State issued a Circular in 1981 outlining the establishment of High Schools, particularly focusing on girls' education. Despite the establishment of 150 schools in the first year, the recognition and regularization of teachers' services became contentious, leading to multiple writ petitions filed by teaching and non-teaching staff. The Patna High Court's Full Bench ruled that the establishment of schools was a continuous process and that the criteria for teacher recognition should apply uniformly across all Project Schools. The State challenged this ruling in the Supreme Court, arguing that only a fraction of the schools had been officially recognized. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's findings, emphasizing the need for equitable treatment of teachers and the importance of the right to education as a fundamental right. The court directed the State to implement the Full Bench's findings within four months, ensuring that all teachers' claims for recognition and regularization were examined fairly. The decision reinforced the State's responsibility to provide education and protect the rights of teachers in Project Schools. Headnote A) Constitutional Law - Right to Education - Fundamental Right - Article 21A of the Constitution of India - The court recognized the fundamental right to education for children aged 6 to 14 years and emphasized the State's duty to provide education as a sovereign function. Held that the establishment of Project Schools was a necessary step to fulfill this constitutional mandate (Paras 1-2). B) Administrative Law - Recognition of Teachers - Regularization of Services - The court held that the provisions governing recognition and regularization of teachers' services in Project Schools must apply uniformly to all schools established under the same scheme, ensuring no discrimination among teachers based on arbitrary criteria (Paras 6-7). C) Education Policy - Establishment of Schools - The court upheld the State's policy decision to establish High Schools in educationally backward areas, emphasizing the need for affirmative action in education for women and children (Paras 3-5). D) Judicial Review - Conflicting Orders - The court noted the conflicting decisions from the High Court regarding the recognition of schools and directed that individual cases be examined in light of the Full Bench's findings to ensure fair treatment of all teachers (Paras 8-9). national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for a series of development projects worth more than 13,000 crore rupees across Tamil Nadu at an event held at IIT-Madras in Chennai today. The projects span road and rail transport, port infrastructure, petroleum and scientific research. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was also present on the occasion. The projects include National Highway works worth around 3,700 crore rupees, initiatives at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V. O. Chidambaranar Port, and the development of railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme. Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Modi described the inauguration of projects worth 13-thousand crore rupees in Tamil Nadu as a historic occasion, saying the initiatives will improve connectivity, strengthen industry and trade, and create employment opportunities for the state’s youth. Mr. Modi said the projects will make daily travel easier and support the state’s economic growth. Recalling his interactions with former Tamil Nadu Chief Ministers M. Karunanidhi and J. Jayalalithaa, Mr. Modi said he had also worked with former Chief Ministers O. Panneerselvam, Edappadi K. Palaniswami and M. K. Stalin during his tenure as Prime Minister. He said that despite changes in governments, his commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and the welfare of its people had remained unchanged. He added that he would continue this journey in cooperation with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Recalling his journey in public service, Mr. Modi said he had completed 25 years as head of government, having taken the oath as Gujarat Chief Minister in October 2001 before becoming Prime Minister. Mr. Modi said India’s progress draws strength from its rich cultural heritage, scientific achievements and modern infrastructure. He cited Tamil Nadu’s temples, scientific institutions and Metro rail network as examples of how tradition and modern development can go hand in hand. The Prime Minister also extended Navaratri greetings to the people of the state. Mr. Modi also dedicated to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras. The centre is part of a pioneering scientific initiative to map more than 100 human brains and create three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution. The research will cover the entire human lifespan, from the foetal stage to old age. The Prime Minister also released C-STROKE, a unique atlas of the human brain affected by ischaemic stroke. Featuring more than 1,000 annotated microscopic sections, the atlas is expected to help researchers worldwide identify new targets for treatment. Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase Two of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around 4,900 crore rupees. The Prime Minister and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay jointly flagged off the new Metro services and travelled on the train. The newly inaugurated stretch is part of Corridor Four of Phase Two. It includes 11 elevated Metro stations spread across approximately 15 kilometres. The projects are aimed at strengthening transport connectivity, improving infrastructure and advancing scientific research in Tamil Nadu.
